newsitem.title: USA: Brooke will enforce existing tobacco pact.
newsitem.headline: Brooke will enforce existing tobacco pact.

text.p: The effect of Friday's mass tobacco litigation settlement on the existing settlement pact between Liggett Group Inc and 25 U.S. states remains unclear, Bennett LeBow said.
In a statement released late Friday, LeBow, chairman of Liggett's parent company, Brooke Group Ltd, said his tobacco company intended to fully enforce its existing agreements.
Liggett shocked the legal and tobacco communities in March of 1996 by becoming the first tobacco company to settle its litigation out of court.

"It remains to be seen how Liggett will ultimately be treated in a global settlement, but something would be drastically wrong with the entire process if the one tobacco company that started the process were the only one hurt by it," LeBow said.
"Liggett previously entered into binding tobacco settlement agreements with the attorneys general of 25 states and we fully intend to enforce our legal rights," he said.
